topics.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang returns amid scandal and credit rating warnings
topics.explanation: Jensen Huang has returned as CEO of Nvidia following a brief ouster triggered by reports of personal affairs and potential security risks. S&P Global Ratings warned it may downgrade the company's credit rating due to rising management and governance risks, while shareholders have filed lawsuits over board oversight.
topics.why_it_matters: Leadership stability and corporate governance—the rules by which a company is run—are critical for investor confidence in a firm that anchors the global AI market.

topics.title: Trump administration proposes new tariffs on 14 major trading partners
topics.explanation: The US has announced plans for fresh tariffs on a dozen countries, including a proposed 40% levy on Chinese imports and 20% on the European Union. Trading partners including Singapore and China have expressed disappointment or threatened retaliation, while analysts suggest the move aims to pressure nations into new trade deals.
topics.why_it_matters: Tariffs are taxes on imported goods that can raise costs for businesses and consumers, potentially disrupting global supply chains and trade relationships.

topics.title: US inflation rose to 3.8% in October according to Fed's preferred gauge
topics.explanation: The Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, which the Federal Reserve uses to track price changes, accelerated to an annual rate of 3.8% in October. This higher-than-expected reading comes amid soaring energy prices and rising costs for holiday items like toys and travel.
topics.why_it_matters: Persistent inflation can force the central bank to keep interest rates higher for longer, which increases the cost of borrowing for homes, cars, and business expansion.

topics.title: FCC approves SpaceX plan to launch 1 million data center satellites
topics.explanation: The Federal Communications Commission has authorized SpaceX to deploy a massive constellation of satellites designed to provide orbital AI computing power. The project, known as Starmind, was approved despite opposition from rivals like Amazon and concerns regarding orbital debris and scientific research.
topics.why_it_matters: This massive expansion of space infrastructure could transform global internet and AI processing capabilities, though it faces significant regulatory and environmental scrutiny.

topics.title: US-backed consortium led by Todd Boehly to buy Lukoil's international assets
topics.explanation: A group of investors including billionaire Todd Boehly and the US International Development Finance Corp has signed a deal to acquire the international oil and gas assets of Russia's Lukoil. The transaction involves a share swap intended to move these energy assets out of Russian control amid ongoing international sanctions.
topics.why_it_matters: This deal represents a significant shift in global energy ownership, moving major oil and gas infrastructure into Western-aligned hands.

topics.title: UK discount retailer Poundland enters administration putting 11,000 jobs at risk
topics.explanation: The major British discount chain Poundland has collapsed into administration after its owners failed to secure a buyer or new funding. The move threatens thousands of jobs and highlights the ongoing struggle for high-street retailers facing rising costs and shifting consumer habits.
topics.why_it_matters: Administration is a legal process where an insolvent company is managed by professionals to pay off debts, often resulting in store closures or the sale of the business.

topics.title: State attorneys general move to block Character.AI from selling user chat data
topics.explanation: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is intervening in Character.AI's bankruptcy proceedings to prevent the company from auctioning off private user data. The AGs allege that the company plans to sell sensitive chat logs, including those belonging to millions of minors, as part of its liquidation process.
topics.why_it_matters: This case highlights the legal risks surrounding data privacy and how personal information is treated when technology companies fail financially.
